title: a merge card explains each change point and its door: the spec explain carries change points (intent, how, files, tests) and a one-way or two-way door with its reason and rollback, plus a comprehension check for a one-way door; fm-decide attaches the code hunks and test lines of each change point from the pull request at the expected head; the board walks intent → spec line → code → test, marks the door, and the server refuses A on a one-way card until every intent is marked reviewed and the check is answered correctly
acceptance: Why. The captain approved the board prototype on 2026-10-07: "看板樣式可以了, 可以以這個版本開發". In the review rounds before that, the captain asked, verbatim: "文字和diagram圖片還是沒有講解改造細節, 也沒有對回原始intent需求, 每一個改造點也沒有連結回相關的github code snippet和tests位置", "意圖對齊要能引導船長看懂改造有符合當初的意圖, spec能對上, 引導船長要細看的話要去哪裡看實際這一段的程式改了什麼? 相關的testcase是什麼?" and "標註這個PR上線的話是一個單向門還是雙向門, 雙向門還有機會rollback, 單向門建議船長細看看懂, 如何在選項引導船長確認自己有看懂?". The prototype's data shapes, UX walkthrough and rendering are in the round's local brief (firstmate records state/briefs/T-242.design.md); its code is reference only. Later that day the captain added, verbatim: "船員名冊顯示的太窄, 高度太限縮, 閱讀順序應該是先看意圖重點列表, 再帶到動畫邏輯帶看"; this task builds the intent key-point walk with code and test links, and the per-block diff walk and the animated hero scene, with links from each intent row into them, follow in T-244. Base note: T-245 is merged; board.js, board.css, intent rows and decision bars exist. T-246 must merge before T-242 implementation because its tabs/sheets share these files. Re-preflight against that base. Normative visual requirements are all stated here: intent key points first; evidence (intent, spec acceptance, named tests, door reason and rollback) is visible without expanding code; each code section starts closed; comprehension is answerable from evidence alone. The local prototype brief is reference only and need not exist in an isolated checkout. T-244 owns animation and per-block diff walkthrough.

Change 1, explain schema (bin/lib/fm_ste.py, bin/lib/fm_spec_preflight.py). check-explain and check-details accept three optional per-locale fields. `change_points`: a list, one item per change point, `{intent: N, how: text}` where N names an existing Intent N of the same locale and `how` is one STE fact sentence; both locales have the same count and the same intent numbers. `door`: `{kind: 'one-way'|'two-way', reason: text, rollback: text}` with the same kind in both locales; `rollback` is required for two-way and may say what cannot be undone for one-way. `check`: `{q: text, options: [text, text, ...2-4], why: text, about: {intent: N}}` present only when the door is one-way and required then. Every text is checked by the existing STE rules and limits. A locale-free top-level spec field `change_refs` (fm_spec_preflight validates it; bin/lib/fm_config_tasks.py keeps calling only check_explain, which is intended: fm_spec_preflight and fm-decide are where the cross-field rules are enforced) lists, index-aligned with change_points, `{files: [repo paths], tests: [{file, name}], acceptance: [0-based indices into the spec's acceptance list]}`, and a top-level `check_answer` holds the 0-based correct option index; preflight refuses an acceptance index or a check_answer index out of range, a change_refs length that differs from change_points, or a one-way door with no check. All three fields stay optional: specs and cards without them are valid as today. The new fields are added to fm_ste's known explain and card fields but not to the fields check-details requires on every merge card, so existing merge cards stay valid; bin/fm-decide.sh's own copy of the field list (around line 413) gets the same three names.

Change 2, the card takes the spec's walk (new bin/lib/fm_card_refs.py, bin/fm-decide.sh). On `fm-decide.sh --request --kind merge --pr N --expected-head SHA`, fm-decide reads the task's spec the way fm_binding does: the pin from Pins(env, task).resolve(if_present=True), or, when no pin exists, the self project spec committed at SHA and the external project spec in private FM_TASKS_DIR; a corrupt pin exits 65 with no card. If the spec explain has change_points, fm-decide puts the spec's change_points, door and check of each locale onto the card details itself (firstmate does not author them); the card's own `intent` items must equal the spec explain's intent items in each locale (same count, same text), and details that already carry any of the three new fields must equal the spec's, or fm-decide exits 65 with a message naming the mismatch and writes no card; a details file with no intent fields at all, for a task whose spec has change_points, also exits 65 asking firstmate to author the intent card from the spec; a card details file with change_points whose spec has none, or a one-way spec door without check_answer, also exits 65. check-details then runs as today on the result. After check-details, fm-decide runs fm_card_refs.py and adds one locale-free top-level details field `refs`, which STE never checks: `{spec_url, acceptance: [the spec's acceptance lines], points: [one per change point: {acceptance: [indices], code: [...], tests: [...]}]}`. fm_card_refs.py runs `gh pr view N --repo <project github> --json headRefOid` through the existing gh wrapper (FM_GH), then `gh pr diff N --repo <project github>`, then the view again, and exits 65 (fm-decide writes no card) unless both views report SHA; `code` holds, for each listed file, each hunk of that diff as `{file, start, end, url, snippet}` for added/context text hunks (the Diff completeness clause defines other kinds) with url `https://github.com/<repo>/pull/N/files#diff-<sha256(path)>R<start>`, at most 12 added or context lines in snippet, and over 20 hunks per change point truncated with a `more` count; `tests` holds, for each `{file, name}`, the line where the name first appears in `git show SHA:<file>` in the project's clone, as `{file, line, name, url}` with a blob URL at SHA, or `line: null, url: null` when the name is absent or git show fails. For the self project spec_url is the spec's blob URL at SHA; for an external project, whose pinned spec lives in private state, spec_url is null and the acceptance lines show as text, so no generated private storage link reaches the card. fm-decide copies the spec's `check_answer` into the pending record as a top-level field `check_answer`, never inside details. `gh pr diff` and the two `gh pr view` calls are new network reads of this command. fm-decide refuses (exit 65) change_points, door or check in the details of every other card kind, including merge-untracked, dispatch, choice, readiness and repin cards. The enriched details are written to a temporary file before the payload is built, and fm_card_refs.py never names both fm-decide and --request (tests/decide.test.sh's raiser sweep).

Change 3, the server enforces the door (board/server.ts). The check is a comprehension prompt, not a secret: the answer stays readable in the committed spec (spec_url) and through the localhost /file route, and that is accepted. The board still does not hand it to the page unasked: the server removes `check_answer` where it sends pending items (/api/state and SSE; pending() itself keeps it for POST /decisions), and /api/task and publicDecision never include it. POST /decisions on a card whose details.en.door.kind is one-way, when the answer would merge (the effect the server derives for that choice is merge, whatever the letter; a choice recorded as change because a question got No does not merge and needs no check), requires `reviewed_intents` (every intent number of the card) and `check_answer` equal to the pending record's `check_answer`; otherwise it answers 409 with code `doorUnconfirmed` and records nothing. The recorded decision keeps `reviewed_intents` and `check_ok: true`. Two-way cards, cards with no door (every card raised before this task) and answers that do not merge are unchanged.

Change 4, the card (board/public/index.html and board.js). On a card with change_points, the intent key-point list (today built by intentBody() in board/public/index.html under the intentHeading and alignmentHeading keys; T-245 nests the done items under the intent rows) becomes a guided walk, read first as the captain asked: one step per Intent N; each step opens first to its evidence view: its spec acceptance lines (refs.points[i].acceptance into refs.acceptance, linked by spec_url when present), each change point's `how` sentence, its tests (file:line, name, link) and the card's CI and review status; the code hunks (file:line, the snippet, a link to the PR diff) sit in a collapsed 'Show code' section under each change point, closed by default on every card including one-way doors, and open only on click; each step ends with an 'I checked this intent' tick. The door shows as a badge (one-way in flag red, two-way in kelp) with the reason, and the rollback for two-way. For a one-way door the decision bar locks A and says what is missing (unticked intents, the unanswered question) until every intent is ticked and the question is answered; a wrong answer shows the card's `why` without scolding. The page sends `reviewed_intents` and `check_answer` with A; the server's answer is the authority. Cards without the new fields render as before. The task detail panel (intentBody's second caller, index.html around line 951) shows the same walk read-only for a merge card with refs (no ticks, no lock), and for a spec explain with change_points but no refs it lists each change point's `how` under its Intent N with no code or test links. The door badge, reason and rollback are part of the evidence view. The comprehension check is answerable from the evidence view alone: fm_spec_preflight refuses a spec whose check names no intent, acceptance line or test that the evidence view shows (the check carries `about: {intent: N}` and its question and answer must be stated in that intent's acceptance lines or its change points' `how`), and A unlocks after the intents are ticked and the check is answered, without any 'Show code' section ever being opened.

Docs. design/design.md §8 'The captain's board' (the captain card) and §5.2 (the explain paragraph and the check-details merge rules): edit in place for change_points, door, check, change_refs and check_answer, the refs attached at the head, the server-side door check and the stripped answer. skills/firstmate/SKILL.md: when writing a spec, judge the door (a stored-format change, a published external write or a force-push of a shared branch is one-way) and write change_points, change_refs and, for a one-way door, the check.

Schema combinations and indices, normative clarification. The complete absence of change_points, door, check, change_refs and check_answer remains legacy behavior. Nonempty change_points requires door and nonempty index-aligned change_refs; orphan fields are refused. Every intent has at least one point; duplicate intent references are allowed for distinct change points. Intent numbers are integers (not bool), 1-based in range; acceptance indices and check_answer are integers (not bool), 0-based in range. Both locales have matching point counts/intent sequence, door kind, check option count/order meaning and about.intent. One-way requires nonempty rollback text stating the irreversible consequence, check and check_answer. Two-way requires nonempty concrete rollback text and forbids check/check_answer. check.options has 2–4 nonempty STE strings. check.about.intent is required and valid. Validation runs before any publication; add positive and each negative combination to STE/preflight/decide fixtures.

Evidence-only deterministic support. check.about.intent associates the question with one intent; in each locale the correct option text must occur verbatim as a nonempty substring in that intent's visible text, its change-point how text, door.reason or door.rollback. check.why cannot be the sole source because it is not visible before the check. Preflight validates both locales using the shared check_answer; wrong-index, absent-evidence, invalid-intent and supported-answer cases are explicit. Independent reviewer also checks whether bilingual options correspond and whether the question truthfully tests that evidence; structural substring support is not a semantic verdict.

Correct-answer protocol, selected contract. Preserve the approved requirement that the merge-effect control stays locked until every intent is reviewed and the answer is correct. Add POST /decisions/check-door with captain authentication and the same origin/session guards as /decisions. Body contains decision id, reviewed intent numbers and answer index. Read the current pending card and return {ok:true} only for a valid complete one-way confirmation; otherwise return {ok:false,code:'doorUnconfirmed',why:<localized text>}. This route never records an answer, writes decision/event state or runs merge/effect commands. Do not return check_answer. The browser sends this check after confirmation changes; pending/incomplete/wrong responses keep every merge-effect control locked. Bind the response to the current decision confirmation values; changes or stale responses invalidate it. Final POST /decisions still independently rechecks the submitted reviewed set/answer against its current pending record. An existing No response producing effect change bypasses the merge-door requirement. Non-A merge letters receive identical checks; A with non-merge effect does not. Direct POST failures leave no writes or merge side effects. Add route/auth/state and e2e wrong→correct/changed-input/stale-response cases.

Stored-answer validity, both routes. On a one-way card requiring confirmation, POST /decisions/check-door and final merge-effect POST /decisions refuse a missing, null, boolean, noninteger or out-of-range stored check_answer with HTTP409 {ok:false,code:'doorUnconfirmed',why:<locale check.why>}. Missing/malformed submitted answer receives the wire-contract malformed response. Both routes validate storage before claiming confirmation. No refusal creates a decision file/directory, emits a decision/merge event or invokes an effect. tests/board-state.test.sh separately covers every stored-invalid shape and omitted submitted answer through both routes; the final write must remain after validation.

Exact check-route wire contract. POST /decisions/check-door accepts JSON {id:string, reviewed_intents:number[], check_answer:number, locale:'en'|'zh-TW'|'zh-CN'}. reviewed_intents contains unique 1-based intent numbers in range; order is immaterial and normalizes ascending. bool, noninteger, duplicates, out-of-range entries and nonarray are malformed. A valid incomplete set is unconfirmed. check_answer is a 0-based integer, not bool, in the stored question option range. Both check route and POST /decisions use these same field names/normalization; final route retains existing chosen/text/answers fields. locale absent defaults to configured captain language; unsupported/type-invalid locale is malformed. en and zh-TW use their card check.why; zh-CN applies the existing Traditional-to-Simplified conversion, with no new external dependency. Auth/origin/session refusal uses existing guard/status semantics. Invalid JSON/shape/id syntax/locale or missing submitted confirmation fields returns400 {ok:false,code:'doorUnconfirmed',why:<localized check.why when pending available, otherwise localized generic confirmation message>}; unknown id404 {ok:false,code:'decisionMissing'}; valid incomplete/wrong answer or malformed stored answer409 {ok:false,code:'doorUnconfirmed',why:<localized text>}; success200 {ok:true,id:<id>}. An already-recorded id on the check route returns409 {ok:false,code:'decisionAlreadyRecorded'} without mutation. All responses use JSON and never expose stored answer. The final POST retains existing response envelopes for success/existing non-door errors but uses these malformed/unconfirmed confirmation statuses. Tests cover en/zh-TW/zh-CN feedback, omitted locale/default, unsupported locale, all malformed fields, reordered complete set, incomplete set and non-recording successful check. No state/stream event is emitted by a check. Final-response browser normalization: before its existing success test `if (!r.error) answered.add(id); sent.delete(id);`, normalize any parsed final response with ok:false into an error result using localized why (or localized fallback), preserving code and confirmation inputs. Keep that existing success/lock sequence and the unchanged tests/board-card-layout.test.sh assertion valid. On final400/409 after a successful check-route verification, never add answered, clear picks/drafts/reviewed intents/answer, or hide the card; clear in-flight state, invalidate stale confirmation, display localized feedback and leave the same card pending and retryable. Add scoped E2E cases for successful verification followed by final400 and409 in both locales, retaining inputs and recovering with new confirmation, and preserve legacy r.error,403 and unreachable handling.

Diff completeness. Paths are repository-relative normalized POSIX paths: refuse absolute paths, dot/dotdot segments, NUL/control characters, duplicates and invalid decoding. Decode Git C-quoted path headers (including escaped Unicode bytes) correctly; URL percent-encode repository path segments while computing diff anchor SHA256 from the actual UTF-8 path. Parse text hunks with old/new ranges. Added/context snippets use right-side R anchors; deletion-only hunks use old-side L anchors with at most12 removed/context lines and side:'left'. Existing file deletion links remain PR-diff links, not nonexistent head blobs. Binary and rename-only changes produce a link with kind:'binary' or kind:'rename', null start/end and empty snippet; no invented code lines. Match listed files against either old or new normalized path, include each once, and refuse a listed code file absent from the diff with exit65. Truncate over20 entries per point with point.more equal omitted count. Test quoted/space/non-ASCII paths, traversal rejection, deletions, binary, rename-only, absent files and URL encoding. Missing named test gets line:null and url:null; distinguish that valid helper result from failed helper launch.

Privacy boundary. Local private cards may display authored acceptance/explain prose, including private path text when intentionally authored. The helper never generates an external spec storage path/link; external spec_url is null. All generated source/test URLs contain validated repository-relative paths and expected head. Add captured-gh-arguments/public-write and URL assertions; do not claim to scrub arbitrary locally displayed authored prose.

Confirmation replay/idempotency. After a successful one-way merge-effect decision, store normalized reviewed_intents, check_ok:true and a private door_confirmation_fingerprint equal to SHA256 of canonical compact JSON {reviewed_intents:<sorted unique list>,check_answer:<submitted integer>}. Never return this fingerprint through state/SSE/task/publicDecision.
